author: Patrick Hite
title: Retired Staunton superintendent publishes book on school leadership - NewsBreak
text:
By Patrick Hite ,
20 hours ago
STAUNTON — When Garett Smith retired as superintendent of Staunton City Schools, he knew he wasn't finished with education. He began his own consulting firm, Garett Smith Educational Solutions LLC, as well as writing his first book, "Simple Solutions to Stubborn School Problems: A 70 in 7 Journey."
The book just published and is now available through both his website or on most websites that sell books, including Amazon and Books-A-Million . He co-authored it with Stenette Byrd III, a friend and former co-worker of Smith's, and the chief of schools for Suffolk Public Schools.
Smith said Byrd had been pushing him to write a book for a number of years. Smith finally decided to take the leap when he retired from Staunton City Schools.
The book is for any educator getting ready to start a new school year, but Smith said it's also for parents and students interested in the educational system.
More: Heifetz Institute's summer festival celebrates 30th anniversary
The book takes a deep dive dive into crucial areas like student success, looking at how educators can help every child consistently attend, behave positively, and achieve their full learning potential.
Smith said the book also explores what it takes to build a thriving school culture, a place where everyone feels safe, respected, and excited to learn. Smith also advocates in the book for continuous improvement and always striving to be better in an effort to empower every student to reach new heights.
The book is divided into three parts: "Kindness Matters," "ABC Student Success Plans" and "A Cycle of Continuous School Improvement."
The first part includes a story on Smith dealing with the death of one of his students, the name change of the high school in Staunton, educating students during COVID and, one of Smith's lasting legacies in Staunton, the Kindness Matters campaign.
The other two sections focus on developing student success plans and finding ways to help schools improve.
"It's a lot about the power of classroom presence," Smith said. "I've heard all the reasons why administrators can't get into classrooms and I don't buy any of them. That's the meat of the work, the instruction in the classroom. That's where the rubber meets the road. If you want to improve schools you need to know what's happening in every classroom."
Smith just wanted an avenue to share stories that he thought could help educators. This book provided that avenue.
"This isn't just a book of ideas," according to the back cover of the book. "It's a guide to taking effective action. It's about empowering you to create the kind of educational environment where every student, every day, has the chance to succeed."
More: Roach, Troxell twins lead Wilson tennis into regional quarterfinals
One thing he found out when he started writing the book was that he didn't like sitting in front of a computer screen, even though he did for much of his educational career. So he learned to do voice to text and would walk around Gypsy Hill Park as he spoke his book into existence.
"Then I figured out once I got a manuscript how to put it in Google Books and walk around and listen to it," Smith said. "Then I'd stop and make notes on my phone where I needed to make edits. It wasn't that bad of a process."
In addition to his own firm and his book, Smith began working in January with both the Aspiring Superintendents and the Recently Appointed Administrators programs through Virginia Tech, helping train future school leaders.
"I like to get into doing more direct school turnaround work with school divisions," Smith said. "Hopefully I can do that next year. I think that is what we specialized in in Staunton."
